note:
escalations is the ratchet. It counts write-shaped capabilities the table grants and the hardcoded checks deny. The ratchet only shrinks: a rise fails the gate, and a fall fails it too until re-banked, because a ratchet nobody re-banks stops ratcheting.

2026-08-25 RE-BANK, 28 -> 24. It went 28 -> 34 first, and that rise was NOT data drift: the rows were unchanged and 6bbdae50 (the field-officer caseload UI) rewrote crm7's src/hooks/usePermissions.ts after the previous bank, tightening the hardcoded model so six previously-matched grants became denied. crm7 migration 20260912000000 then revoked the ten capabilities that were not a question — every '.write' held by the role literally named 'viewer', 20 rows across both tenants — which took it to 24, below the old bank.

COMPARABLE CELLS ROSE 168 -> 196 in the same window, because the same commit added roles to the shared set. So the ratio improved more than the raw number suggests: 28/168 to 24/196.
not_a_defect_count: A divergence is a question, not a defect. Either the table is wrong or the hardcoded check is, and deciding that is reconciliation work. This number sizes the work; it does not accuse either side.

what_the_24_are.member: 10 — arguable. A member writing contacts is a product question, not a defect.
what_the_24_are.gto_staff: 4 — probably correct; day-to-day GTO operators do write.
what_the_24_are.field_manager: 5 — arguably SHOULD be granted. The operator's own description of the role is that it edits caseloads across field officers, so the hardcoded side may be the one that is behind.
what_the_24_are.viewer: 0 — settled 2026-08-25. A role named 'viewer' holding a write was indefensible under any model, so it was the only group revoked without asking.

deliberately_not_reconciled: The remaining 24 are Braden's authorisation model. Clearing a red check is not a reason to change it, and this file exists to SIZE that work rather than to license doing it unilaterally.
